source.publication: 2025 Montana Individual Income Tax Return Form 2 and Form 2 Instructions
source.section: Form 2 PDF p1 lines 1-8 and PDF p2 worksheet lines 1-13; Instructions PDF p12-13 lines 1-8; PDF p17 tax calculation; PDF p18 rate tables

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 43,700.00 + wages (person 1) 30,000.00 = 73,700.00. Federal taxable income = 73,700.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 42,200.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Filing status married filing jointly, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 73,700.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 31,500.00; line 3 42,200.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 0 x 5,660.00 = 0.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 42,200.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 42,200.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 42,200.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 5.9% x 42,200.00 = 2,489.80, less 506 = 1,983.80; line 13 = 1,983.80, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 42,200.00 = 1,983.40. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 1,983.40. The form gives 1,983.80; expected keeps the projection's 1,983.40, a difference of 0.40 from the table's whole-dollar constant (506 against 506.40). Taxable income is exactly the joint bracket start.
accepted_approximations: The tables print a whole-dollar constant with the 5.9% rate (253, 506, 380) where the bracket arithmetic gives 253.20, 506.40, 380.40.
